open_points.subject: agent instruction protection under standing approval
open_points.text: the agent's instructions are then the only protection
open_points.question: What proves that the required room-naming instruction is installed, current and applied to this agent execution, and what happens if that cannot be proved before a standing-approved room write?
options: Kernel refuses or pauses the write unless the required instruction version is verified
Release admission verifies installation once; executions perform no check
No verification is performed and Registry accepts any name the agent submits
open_points.default_guess: Kernel refuses the write unless the required instruction version is verified.

witness.initial: An add-room node has standing approval, but the agent runs without the required naming instruction or with an older copy.
events: The agent chooses a room name containing a person's health condition.
Cabinet Kernel executes the standing-approved node without showing the exact request to the owner.
outcomes: The write is stopped because the required instruction cannot be verified.
The room is written because Registry checks no name content and the standing approval bypasses exact-request review.
witness.observer: The owner and anyone receiving the agent projection see whether the room exists and exposes the condition.

open_points.subject: standing approval scope
open_points.text: Under a standing approval for that node (K-08)
open_points.question: Exactly which future executions and inputs does the standing approval authorize, how long does it last, and when does revocation take effect?
options: It authorizes every input to that node only in the named immutable flow version until explicitly revoked
It authorizes only inputs satisfying constraints recorded with the approval
It expires after a defined time or number of executions
It authorizes the logical node across later flow versions
open_points.default_guess: Authorize every input to that node only in the named immutable flow version until explicitly revoked, with revocation effective before the next execution.

witness.initial: The owner has given standing approval to an add-room node and the flow or its requested room name later changes.
events: The agent runs the node with the changed input.
Kernel evaluates the existing standing approval.
outcomes: Kernel treats the approval as still covering the execution and writes the room without exact-request review.
Kernel treats the approval as expired or outside scope and waits for the owner's approval of the exact request.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a new approval prompt or an unprompted room.

open_points.subject: prohibition on standing-approved repeated writes
open_points.text: the governance's rule against a standing approval for a Registry write inside a map over a collection (R0-99) still holds
open_points.question: What precisely counts as "inside a map over a collection," including nested flows, loops, recursion and repeated node invocation, and which component must prevent or revoke a prohibited standing approval?
options: Kernel detects every construct capable of repeated collection-driven execution and refuses the standing approval
Only an explicit syntactic map node is covered and Kernel enforces that case
The rule is procedural for the owner and no component enforces it
open_points.default_guess: Kernel refuses standing approval for any node reachable through collection-driven repeated execution, including nested flows.

witness.initial: An add-room node is reached repeatedly through a nested subflow rather than a syntactically direct map node.
events: The owner attempts to give the node standing approval.
The flow processes a collection and invokes the node once per item.
outcomes: Kernel classifies the nested repetition as being inside a map and refuses the standing approval.
Kernel treats only a direct map child as covered and writes every room without exact-request review.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a refused standing approval or multiple unreviewed rooms.
